generated_note: Synthesis of 6 cluster scorecards (C1-C6) covering all 402 C++ test files. FIND-AND-DOCUMENT only; no product/test code modified.

ranked_weak_findings.user_visible_failure_missed: A regression re-introducing any of 21 replayed CVEs -- connecting to the attacker SMB share (CVE-2018-4993 NTLM leak), executing embedded /AA JavaScript (CVE-2021-30560), running injected font PostScript (CVE-2024-4367) -- ships GREEN as long as Document::open returns within 5-10s and doesn't throw. The catch-all try/catch (57-59) even hides an outright throw. No test asserts the attack was neutralized.

If MuJS were ever wired to a launch/openDoc transport, app.launchURL('file:///C:/Windows/System32/calc.exe') would spawn a process and this test still passes -- the only oracle is that fireKeystrokeEvent doesn't throw and pageCount() survives. The name promises a block it never verifies.

ranked_weak_findings.test: ImageCommandsDirtyTest.* (15 cases: Insert/Remove/Resize/Rotate/Crop x exec/undo/redo; reps 314,367,417,470,533)
ranked_weak_findings.user_visible_failure_missed: Image insert/remove/resize/rotate/crop are all VISUAL, yet the only oracle is createDisplayList()!=nullptr. A command that no-ops, inserts at the wrong rect/size, rotates the wrong way, crops the wrong region, or an undo that fails to revert — the page still builds a display list, so all 15 stay green. No pixels, geometry, XObject presence, or dirty-state verified.

Replaces a span's first char with 'X', then asserts only EXPECT_NO_THROW + blocksAfter.size()>0. The editor writing the wrong glyph, dropping the edit, mirroring the text, emitting it white/invisible, corrupting position, or clobbering/recoloring NEIGHBOUR spans (the exact shipped ambient-state-leak bug class) — all pass, because the page 'still has some text'.

Feature is glyph horizontal-width scaling. CharRatioLogic recomputes charRatio=oldLen/newLen and asserts it equals oldLen/newLen — calls zero product code. If EditTextCommand's width math were inverted/dropped/clamped (text at half/double width, overlapping or spilling off-line), every assertion here passes. The six *NoException tests read back no Tz/matrix/width/geometry.

Reconstruction writes NEW glyphs into the page content stream (visual). All meaningful assertions are inside if(result.success) and only check originalText/editedText non-empty + bbox w/h>0. Nothing renders/re-extracts the produced PDF. A reconstructor writing wrong/garbage/mirrored/invisible text, or a mutation flipping success to false, passes.

MultiplePageEdits has ZERO assertions after the edits ('without crash' comment) — an edit that no-ops, lands wrong glyphs/position, or corrupts the other page passes. SaveAfterEdit explicitly declines content verification (line 247) and only checks save didn't throw + reopen yields non-empty blocks — a saved PDF dropping/garbling/mirroring/off-page-writing the edit passes.

The ONE end-to-end test of an inherently VISUAL feature (text alignment). The injector could write every block Left-aligned when Center/Right was requested, off-page, or invisible — extractPlainText().find(marker) still succeeds, so it passes. No geometry/x-offset/render oracle exists.

Left/Center/Right alignment is the feature, but only extractPlainText().find(...) is checked. Text drawn left when it should be centered, positioned off-page, white/invisible, or with a leaked CTM all extract identically and pass. MultipleBlocksOnDifferentPages proves presence, never position.

Bold oracle is EXPECT_TRUE(nameMentionsBold || nameDiffers) (266): any font-name change for an unrelated reason (subset prefix, substitution, resource rename) passes as 'bold survived' even if strokes aren't heavier. Font family/size verified only via stext metadata — a correct Tf reference with glyphs rendered invisible/mirrored/white/off-page reports the right font regardless.

Search returning ZERO hits for text actually on the fixture is invisible: BasicSearch asserts only totalMatches()>=0 (a tautology — returns size_t) and the hit-structure/quad-geometry checks live inside for(hit:result.hits) loops that run zero times when empty. Broken indexing/highlight-quads stay green.

File named 'performance' asserts NO timing. Verified: totalMatches() returns int hits.size(), so EXPECT_GE(...,0) is always true. Only real assert is query non-empty. Search returning zero hits for present text, or case-insensitive returning different sets for 'test' vs 'TEST', passes. Quad checks are in a vacuous loop.

These are the comment-labelled 'critical' tests for the Y-flip regression. Each computes the mapping with the test's OWN arithmetic (e.g. pixY=(fitzTopLeft.y-tf.translateY)/tf.scaleY) and asserts on that — never calls mapper_->pdfToPixel / pixelRectToPdf. If the PRODUCT mapper inverts Y (a scanned-text selection lands on the opposite end of the page), the test cannot fail.

Reconstructing text onto a scanned page is visual. execute() is wrapped in EXPECT_NO_THROW; the comment concedes it 'may succeed or fail gracefully'; the only post-state check is image-data SIZE equality after undo. A command that silently does nothing, writes the wrong text, positions it wrong, or an undo restoring a same-size-but-different image all pass.

Per-run font/size emission is visual; oracle is distinct extracted-font-size count (EXPECT_GE(fontSizes.size(),2)). Per-run text rendered with wrong glyphs, wrong X/Y, mirrored, white/invisible, overlapping, or off-page all still yield >=2 distinct extracted sizes and pass. Emitted operators never inspected (streams FlateDecode-compressed).

Test name claims bold coverage; the final assert is EXPECT_NE(bytes.find("<w:document"),npos) — a structural shell check unrelated to bold. Bold never emitted into the DOCX (heuristic-to-<w:b/> wiring broken) passes; comment admits 'cannot assert the specific markup'.
Body ends in SUCCEED() ('Soft-asserting'). Undo dropping formatting runs (a blank/de-formatted line) — precisely the UI-TE-UNDO-01 bug named in the test's own header — cannot fail this test.

Edited text rendered mirrored, invisible, white-on-white, wrong size, wrong color, or off-page — extraction-present (find(...)!=npos) sees the codepoints regardless of how/whether they render. The visual correctness of the edit is unverified.

OCR's user-visible truth is the RECOGNIZED TEXT. hocr non-empty + blocks>0 passes even when OCR mis-recognizes the page into gibberish; no assertion checks a KNOWN word from the scanned fixture appears in the hOCR.

Autosave silently fails to capture ANY edit family on crash (the exact data-loss class this project keeps shipping) and every one of the 15 tests stays green: finishRow() records capture_present=NO as passing DATA and the only statement is SUCCEED(). Zero EXPECT_/ASSERT_ in the whole file. A crash-recovery regression that drops all edits produces a green suite.

Optimize (garbage=4) leaves stale/deleted form-field values or removed content embedded in the output; the test reopens and asserts only pageCount>0 (L194), so the exact data-leak the test is NAMED for ships green.

After a save that throws (file locked), undo() can undo the WRONG op / corrupt the page / leave inconsistent edit state and the test stays green — both a clean return and any thrown exception satisfy the oracle. Only a hard crash on an ASan build fails it; on Debug/Release a logic-corrupting rebind passes.

docA and docB are both test_3page.pdf (SetUp L54-57) so changedPages/expectedRegions are 0; the entire change-highlighting path is asserted only against 0==0. A dialog that computes change counts completely wrong for real differing docs passes.

Writer emits a malformed pdfaid part/conformance (part=3, wrong letter). Asserting only that substrings "1" and "B" appear ANYWHERE in the packet (timestamps/UUIDs contain both) cannot detect wrong/missing PDF/A identification. Same pattern L66/68,82/84,98/100,114/116,150/152.

insertBookmark returns true but never inserts the node (or inserts wrong title/index). The test checks only the boolean return and explicitly gives up on the model oracle ('BookmarkPanel doesn't expose manager_', L187), so a no-op insert that returns true passes despite the test name.

Captures textAfter (L68) but NEVER asserts textAfter != textBefore. If replacePage silently no-ops, textAfter==textBefore and the undo round-trip trivially passes — a page-replace that does nothing (user's replacement lost) ships green.

writeMetadata may stage 8 fields in an in-memory dict never serialized on save; readMetadata reads the same in-memory dict so all 8 EXPECT_EQ pass, yet the saved file carries no title/author/dates. Only Title is ever save/reopen-verified (Test 14).

Value equality is checked only against the in-memory FormManager; the field is never saved and reopened. A regression where setFieldValue updates the widget cache but fails to write /V (value lost on save) passes.

The saved file is validated only by reopen + pageCount()==3. A save that rebinds correctly but silently DROPS the created annotation from the written PDF passes (reopened doc still has 3 pages, in-memory undo still decrements). User loses their annotation on disk with a green test.

A malformed font dict that MuPDF parses into a garbage glyph program (wrong widths, missing glyphs, silent .notdef substitution) is never detected — the harness only survives non-crash. A font-parser regression that renders 'Hello' as blank/.notdef passes green. Zero assertions = zero behavioral oracle.

Labelled 'regression test for Karen QA finding #2/#4' but the production CMap-scan code is NEVER called — the test copies the loop into its own body and asserts on that copy. If the real ContentStreamEditor CMap scanner still used unsigned short (the original infinite-loop bug) or mishandled mranges, both tests stay green. Zero coverage of the fix they claim to lock.

Type3FontBuilder writes a CharProc whose inline image is blank, inverted, or from the wrong glyph, OR /Differences maps code 1 to the wrong Unicode name. Every test passes because they only check /Subtype is Type3 and the stream contains 'd0','BI','ID','EI'. User sees garbled/blank/wrong reconstructed Type3 text. Sibling bundler proves the NCC oracle is ~30 lines away.

The ONLY ranking-correctness check (Arial should win when the region was rendered in Arial) is wrapped in if(arialFirst){...}. When the ranker is wrong and Arial does NOT rank first, the EXPECT_GT is skipped and the test passes — the assertion is neutered exactly on the failure case. User editing scanned text gets Times substituted for Arial (serif glyphs).

embedFont allocates 'Fsub0' but writes a malformed/empty FontFile2 stream or drops the glyph program; the PDF opens but embedded text renders as .notdef/tofu. Green because the test only inspects a returned string — it never reopens the doc nor rasterizes a glyph. Below even the reopens-without-error bar.

A subsetting/rasterization defect that maps 'A' to the .notdef box outline (or wrong glyph index) still yields a non-null ARGB32 bitmap of positive size that atlas.contains(U'A') reports true. User sees tofu; oracle asserts only presence+format+size>0, never that the rasterized outline is the letter A.

GlyphSynthesizer's b->d HFlip recipe emits a wrong/garbage/non-mirrored bitmap. Test asserts only ea.contains(U'd') + !d.isNull() + quality>=kMinQualityThreshold (self-computed by the synthesizer). User sees a malformed 'd' in edited scanned text; test stays green. No pixel comparison to a reference d or to HFlip(b).

compose() returns a correctly-sized but BLANK canvas (no glyphs blitted, wrong offsets, all-transparent). Asserts width==200 & height==50 which are the requested INPUTS echoed back. A compositor that draws nothing passes 9 of 12 tests. User sees empty overlay where composited glyphs should be.

Fixture paints three IDENTICAL 15x20 black rectangles for A,B,C. If GlyphAtlas maps codepoints to wrong crop regions (stores 'C' bitmap under key 'A'), every test passes because all three bitmaps are byte-identical. An atlas rendering .notdef or the wrong glyph is indistinguishable from a correct one.

Assertions are success/!isNull/donorUsed==U'd'/quality>0. None inspect pixels. A synthesizer that copies 'd' verbatim WITHOUT the horizontal flip produces a visibly wrong 'b' on the page yet passes. The transform — the entire point of synthesis — is never validated.

if(spinner && spinner->isVisible()){ EXPECT_EQ(min,6); EXPECT_EQ(max,144); } — if the spinner is never created or hidden for FreeText (a real regression), the body is skipped and the test reports GREEN with zero assertions executed. The FreeText font-size control could be fully broken and the suite stays green.

The CNN must DISCRIMINATE Arial (sans) from Times (serif). EXPECT_LT(sim,0.99f) lets a broken/text-dominated embedding scoring ~0.98 for serif-vs-sans pass. A classifier that cannot tell serif from sans -> user gets a serif substitute for a sans source -> wrong glyphs, while the discrimination test stays green. Should assert a real margin (SameFont - DifferentFont > delta).

findMatch(Arial,Bold) silently returns the Regular face; user's bold text renders non-bold. Each test states the behavior in a comment and asserts only familyName non-empty, so weight/style/serif regressions are invisible.

EXPECT_TRUE(allCompliant || !allCompliant) and if(isEmbedded||!isEmbedded) are literal logical tautologies that can never fail. allFontsCompliant() could return the wrong verdict and the test passes. Zero coverage of the compliance decision the user relies on.

renderStyledText ignores the bold flag and the underline (renders plain 'Hello World'); >50 ink pixels still present so it passes. That a bold run is heavier and 'World' is underlined is never verified. Same at 1338 (italic+strikethrough) and 1233 (asserts equal SIZE only).

Substitute-font horizontal scale computed as 1.6x when a true width-match needs 1.05x — substituted text renders ~50% too wide/overlapping. Bound (0.5,2.0) accepts it. No golden per-string width ratio is pinned.

applyEditsWithSubstitution on an embedded CID font produces a stream whose 2-byte CIDs index wrong glyphs (broken Identity-H/CIDToGIDMap). Asserts only no-throw + 'page still has text blocks' + an 'Arial' substring. Extraction round-trip uses ToUnicode, so wrong-glyph-but-right-ToUnicode reads back correct while rendering garbage.

The single decompressed-stream byte-absence assertion (the one test in this file that proves the redacted secret is gone from Flate-compressed content) is GTEST_SKIPPED@67-69 whenever SetUp falls back from test_redaction.pdf to test_single.pdf. In that config a redaction that paints a box but leaves the secret's Tj operators intact ships GREEN. Redacted SSN survives in the saved stream; nothing catches it.

The strongest text-redaction truth oracle (SSN absent from extraction AND decompressed content stream, control survives) GTEST_SKIPs@428-430 unless the fixture is exactly test_redaction.pdf. Under fixture absence the redaction P0 coverage collapses to mark-count/index proxies (UI-RED-01..05) — a real leak escapes green.

The security VERIFIER's own unit file constrains it almost not at all: EXPECT_TRUE(result.success||!result.success)@114-117 and EXPECT_GE(unsigned,0)@119-120 are always-true; ConstructDestroy@41 is SUCCEED(). checkTextRemoved is only ever asserted TRUE (empty/no-text) here; no test in this file asserts it returns FALSE for genuine leftover text on a real PDF. A mutation making checkTextRemoved always-return-true (never detect a leak) passes this entire file — positive detection is caught ONLY in test_redaction_edge_cases:646.

All PDF-path EXIF strips assert only a return bool/count@148,226 and never reopen the saved PDF to inspect the embedded image XObject bytes. A no-op strip that touches the images but removes no GPS/camera metadata passes — the privacy guarantee (EXIF actually gone from the shipped file) is unverified on the real product path (only the in-memory QImage path is checked).

resize/rotate/crop that returns true but does not alter the XObject geometry — or writes a wrong CTM producing a mirrored/half-size image (the exact bug class fixed in a03f6b6/half-size-under-CTM) — passes: the only assertions are EXPECT_TRUE(result) and unchanged count. A no-op is indistinguishable from correct.

The file advertises a 'PdfCanvas rendering oracle' but verifyDisplayListOracle only asserts the display list is non-null@71 — never rasterizes. An image inserted at the wrong position, rotated the wrong way, or rendered invisibly still builds a valid display list and passes. Rotate correctness reduces to CTM-array delta>0.01@123, which any CTM perturbation satisfies.

Text-into-image replacement validated only by echoed struct fields (approach==C, editedText==input)@171-173. If the masker fails to erase the original scanned text, or the new glyphs render blank/mispositioned/mirrored (defects this subsystem has repeatedly hit), the test still reports success.

On any runner lacking tessdata/eng.traineddata or the scanned fixtures (a realistic CI config) ~30-41 of 42 tests GTEST_SKIP and the file reports GREEN with zero image-text-edit verification — a totally broken ImageReplacer ships undetected. No unconditional smoke assertion. Dominant surviving oracle EXPECT_NE(xobjBefore,xobjAfter)@317 proves only that something changed.

The ghost-text renderBbox-union fix AND the pixel-width-expansion formula are re-implemented inside the test body (@286-300, @189-192) then asserted against copies of themselves — production ImageReplacer is never invoked. A regression in the actual union/width path would not fail these tests; they only prove std::min/std::max and ceil() work.

Entire suite only asserts the scanner reports NOTHING on a clean fixture. A ProhibitedFeatureScanner that is broken and never detects encryption/JavaScript/external-refs (always returns false/empty) passes every test -> PDF/A compliance scanning silently passes non-compliant documents with zero test failing.

Certificate trust-chain is NEVER positively validated. Every fixture is self-signed and MuPDF has no system trust-store (noted at 481), so certificateStatus is always non-Okay. The cert-trust tests assert only 'non-Okay OR !certValid OR !isFullyValid', which a self-signed cert satisfies unconditionally -> a signature from an untrusted/attacker-controlled issuer is indistinguishable from a trusted one; a broken trust check is never caught. Plus SUCCEED() early-returns and GTEST_SKIPs.

DocMDP permission ENFORCEMENT is never tested negatively. /DocMDP + /P N are only grep-checked in bytes; the only behavioral tests confirm ALLOWED changes keep the digest valid. There is NO test that a DISALLOWED change (content edit/annotation under P1 NoChanges, content change under P2 FormFillOnly) is FLAGGED as a violation. If enforcement silently permitted forbidden edits, all certification tests stay green while the guarantee is void.

OCSP staleness / CRL nextUpdate-expiry enforcement could be silently removed and these FIX-OCSP-VALIDATOR regression tests still pass, because the self-signed cert with useTrustAnchors=false yields UntrustedChain in ALL cases -> EXPECT_NE(LtvValidated) never depends on the freshness check (the tests' own comments 283-284 concede 'both end up as UntrustedChain'). A signature backed only by a 30-day-stale/expired revocation response could be accepted as fresh in production.

The tamper-injection line has an operator-precedence defect: 'f.write(&b == 0 ? "\x01" : "\x00", 1)' evaluates '&b == 0' (address of a stack var, never null) as always-false, so it unconditionally writes 0x00. If the byte at the 75% offset is already 0x00 the mutation is a no-op and the test asserts !isFullyValid() on an UNMODIFIED validly-signed doc -> a genuinely-broken verifier returning isFullyValid=true fails only by luck of the target byte. A tamper test that may not tamper is security theatre.

The RFC-3161 timestamp-token OID presence is only printed to stdout, never asserted ('bonus best-effort'), and the reachability gate merely checks a local file exists rather than the network. TSA timestamping could be completely non-functional (no token ever embedded) and this real-endpoint test still passes -> an unsigned-time signature presents as timestamped to users.

No test asserts a GOOD OCSP response signed by an UNTRUSTED/arbitrary responder is rejected. Fixtures self-sign the OCSP with the same cert and the code comment (341-342) states verifyWith 'doesn't gate on OCSP signer trust, only the certStatus value'. An attacker who strips the real revoked-status responder and injects a self-signed GOOD OCSP into /DSS would be reported as validly revocation-checked. Revoked-path oracle is genuine; the forged-GOOD negative is missing.

A redaction that visually masks but leaves the underlying text/glyphs recoverable in the saved PDF passes, because the only content oracle is absence of the literal string '/UndoStack'. The actual redacted secret is never searched for in the output bytes or extracted text.

SSRF via /GoToR UNC to an attacker SMB share (NTLM leak), an auto-navigable data:text/html script, or a re-exposed submitForm/exportDataObject exfil API would all still pass -- each oracle is only that open/render/fireKeystroke didn't throw. Names promise 'Rejected/NotExecuted/NotAvailable' the tests never verify.

NO test in any encryption file proves a permission-restricted operation is actually blocked. Every 'permission' assertion is a getPermissions() bitmask read-back. If a downstream copy/print path ignored the flag, or saveEncrypted wrote permission bits without binding them to the crypto dict, the user's copy/print restriction would silently not be enforced and all tests still pass. The test name literally says 'Enforced' while only reading the flag.

An image watermark applied to EVERY page (range filter broken) or to NO page passes: the only assertions are Document::open!=null and pageCount==3. The named even-pages-only contract is asserted nowhere -> a logo could be stamped on confidential pages meant to be excluded, suite green.

The highlight/text-markup tool never actually selects text (empty quads), so no annotation is created on drag -- the user drags over text and gets nothing. The only type assertion is inside 'if(annotationWasCreated)', so the completely-broken tool passes with zero assertions.

After save/reopen a FreeText box shows the wrong font, wrong size, or lost text color: the test set Helv/14.0/red but only asserts daFontName non-empty and daFontSize>0, and never checks daColor. Garbage-but-non-empty DA ships green.

Name claims it verifies hidden OFF-layer OCG text is NOT exposed, but body only asserts Document::open+createDisplayList don't throw. A regression leaking the 'SECRET HIDDEN' string from an OFF optional-content group via text extraction passes green — an information-disclosure defect.

Test computes effectiveZoom=baseZoom*dpr and deviceTileSize=TILE_SIZE*dpr in the test body and asserts them ==2.0/==1024. No PdfCanvas/TileRenderer code runs; if the real renderer forgot to multiply tile dims by DPR, HiDPI pages render at half resolution (blurry) and this stays green.

Computes expectedX=col*TILE_SIZE/zoom itself and asserts ==768 — never calls TileRenderer/RenderTask. If the renderer's real tile->PDF-rect math is wrong (mis-mapped tiles, wrong zoom division), pages render shifted/blank and the test still passes.

tsaGroup QGroupBox exists but its checkbox/URL edit could be unwired: user enables RFC-3161 timestamping, TSA URL is ignored, signature is saved WITHOUT a trusted timestamp -> LTV/long-term validity silently absent. Green because only container objectName is checked.
calculateAll() could compute nothing (or wrong totals) and the test still passes — sole assertion is no-throw. A form whose Total field never recalculates after edits ships green.

EXPECT_TRUE(result || !result) is a tautology passing for ANY bool. A field-validation script that wrongly accepts/rejects input is invisible. FireFormatEvent (line 257) has the identical formatted.empty()||!formatted.empty() defect for currency/date format output.

Every File/Edit/View/Pages action can exist by objectName yet be connected to no/wrong slot (Save/Open/Find do nothing when clicked); all 22 tests still pass. Nothing invokes an action and asserts a document/state change.

calculationOrderAction exists with correct text but triggered() connected to nothing/wrong slot — clicking the menu item does nothing. File is NAMED 'menu_wiring' yet never triggers the wire. Same defect for altTextAction (line 120).

Sets HideStickyNotes then asserts only createDisplayList returns non-null. If the filter silently fails to remove sticky-note annotations, the display list is still non-null and the test passes — the user-visible 'sticky notes disappear' is never checked with a pixel/annotation-count oracle.

Builds H1+P+Figure(altText='Test image') but asserts only hasStructureTree()==true after reopen. If buildTree drops the Figure, loses altText, or writes every node as /P, the PDF fails accessibility/screen-reader use while the test stays green.

successCount++ runs even when Document::open returns null (if(doc) only guards render); sole assertion successCount+exceptionCount==5 is always true if threads finish. Malicious PDF failing to open, corrupt tiles, or cross-thread state bleed all pass — the stated 'no inter-thread corruption' goal is never checked.

Despite the 'render' filename, no pixels are rendered — oracle is extractPlainText().find. Misses the small-text edit landing mirrored, wrong-color, wrong-position, wrong-glyph, or off-page (only detects a total no-op).
Asserts only PK zip-magic + part-name/<sheetData> substring presence. Sheets exported structurally valid but EMPTY or with garbled/wrong cell values (no PDF-derived value reaches the sheet) pass.

EXPECT_GE(ch.quad.width(),0.0) / height()>=0.0 accept zero — a mutation collapsing every character quad to zero area (all glyphs stacked at a point / degenerate positioning, breaking selection & highlight) passes. Only fontSize>0 is a real check.

PreservesRendering asserts only pageCount()>0 — if BDC injection corrupts the content stream so the page renders blank/garbled, page count is unaffected. MultipleRegions asserts only pageHasMarkedContent==true — a tagger emitting P where H1 was requested, dropping regions, or wrong MCIDs (wrong document structure / reading order for assistive tech) passes.

Intends to prove non-last lines get positive word-spacing, but body.find(" Tw\n") is a substring of "0 Tw\n" (the leading space). If the justifier is broken and emits 0 Tw on every line, both finds succeed — fully un-justified text (renders left-aligned) passes green.

The real checks (selected text == region text; quads cover the glyphs) are wrapped in if(!isEmpty) guards / empty-loops. A regression where selection silently returns empty text or zero quads for a text-bearing region passes because the assertions are skipped.

The color edit could drop the rg operator, mirror the text, or apply the wrong color — it produces wrong output without throwing, so both pass. (Mitigated at file level by ColorPersistsThroughSaveAndReopen:243 which counts red pixels — but these two contribute zero oracle value.)
Comment states expected ~2550x3300, but the assertion is >100 on each axis. A DPI regression (renders at 72 DPI ~612x792, or a thumbnail) passes, silently degrading OCR input quality.

sawPositionalForm is set if any shaped glyph id is absent from the isolated-cmap nominal set — verifies substitution happened, not that it was CORRECT. Shaping emitting wrong positional forms or garbage gids (also not in nominal set) passes; joined Arabic could render incorrectly.
Despite the name, only EXPECT_NO_THROW({cmd.execute();}) — execute() silently not calling applyEdits, or applying nothing, has no spy or state check to catch it.
Zero EXPECT/ASSERT despite the 'ReturnsValue' name; comment says 'expect a non-null image reference' but never checks it. saveImageXObjectRef returning null (breaking undo capture) passes silently.

Text-color is a visual property; the oracle inspects the internal formattingRuns struct, never a rendered pixel/argb. The color can be recorded correctly in the model yet not actually render (serialization/render break) and the test passes.

Checks bbox y/height stability (catches Tm.d sign flip and Tfs scale) but never asserts glyph direction (ur.x>ul.x). A pure horizontal mirror that preserves bbox height and y slips through; glyph correctness is extraction-present only (122).

The predicate counts ANY pixel != qRgb(255,255,255) as the selection highlight without confirming semi-transparent blue or correct sub-region. A stray caret line, anti-aliased glyph, or a highlight painted in the wrong color/offset registers hits>0. Catches invisible-highlight, misses wrong-color/wrong-position.

save() could silently drop/corrupt page content (wrong text/images, lost annotations) and stay green — it only checks file exists, >0 bytes, reopens non-null (L139-142). Nothing compares any page content or object before/after.
Metadata set in the in-memory model but readMetadata runs on the same live doc (never reopened from disk); a save that drops the metadata edit passes.
Asserts only that toggled radio B != "Off" (L176); never re-reads radio A to confirm it was DESELECTED. A radio group that fails to clear the sibling (the exact bug the test is named for) passes.

Sole real assertion is EXPECT_GE((int)FormFieldType::Signature,0) (L489) — a compile-time tautology — then SUCCEED(); sigCount/totalCount discarded via (void). If getFormFields mis-tags signature widgets the UI dispatches the wrong dialog and this never notices.

The test emits pageMoved(0,2) itself then checks the spy caught (0,2); no drag-drop code path is exercised, so a broken/never-fired reorder handler in PagePanel is undetected — it only proves Qt signal plumbing works. Same for MultiSelectDelete (L316).

Bare try/catch with ZERO assertions. DeletePageCommand at INT_MAX/-1 could delete the wrong page or silently no-op WITHOUT throwing and the test passes; it neither asserts a throw nor that page count is unchanged.

Pages requested reverse {2,1,0} but emitted forward; only pageCount==3 checked, so page-order not being honored ships green. Same class as ExtractPages_Multiple (L61) which can extract the wrong pages.

A willSave/AA script that silently fails to execute passes: the test only asserts fireDocumentEvent doesn't throw (L180-182) and documents it cannot observe the script ran (L139-150). A regression disabling doc-level JS stays green.
Verifies only reopen + pageCount()==3 (L104). A save that drops/mangles page content but preserves the page count passes — no content or object comparison.
Compares test_3page.pdf against itself, expecting similarity~1.0 and changedPages==0. A comparator hardwired to return 1.0/0 changes (i.e. one that never detects any difference) passes this test.

After injected rename failure, the recovery saveAs(otherPath) is checked only by NO_THROW + reopened pageCount>0. The inserted blank page (the edit that would be lost) is never confirmed in otherPath, so a recovery save writing a PRE-EDIT file passes.
Export emits empty-valued fields (what the name forbids). The body admits it can't check content, checks only '<fields>' exists, then SUCCEED() — an export including empty values passes.

The batch action (FlattenAnnotations) silently does nothing or fails; comment 'May succeed or fail depending on file content' (L133) means it asserts only fileResults.size()==1 — an action that never mutates the PDF passes.

Post-move identity asserted only via widthPt/heightPt equality; test_3page.pdf pages share dimensions, so a MovePage landing at the wrong index (or not moving) yields identical dims and passes. No content/label/object identity checked.

Only page 0 and last index are content-checked after a 500-page reversal. A full-rewrite bug that scrambles/duplicates/drops INTERIOR pages survives (pageCount==500 also survives a swap-without-loss).

expectedProbePixelSize() (54-72) is a line-for-line clone of buildOverlayFont's probe-scaling formula. If the production formula computes the wrong pixel size, the test recomputes the SAME wrong value and asserts equality — an overlay glyph rendered at the wrong size passes.

Every test asserts ranked.empty() on a degenerate input; NONE loads a working classifier and checks the ranking is correct. If rankByVisualSimilarity mis-orders candidates when the model IS available, no test fails. The user-facing behavior (correct font for a scanned region) is entirely un-oracle'd.

The coversScript()/no-penalty checks live inside if(!fontFilePath.empty()) + if(prof.has_value()). If the matcher regresses to an empty file path or analyzeFromFile fails, those assertions are silently skipped and the test passes — the Arabic-run-matched-to-a-Latin-font bug this file exists to catch slips through.

resolve('Arial') returning the WRONG file (any non-empty path, e.g. comic.ttf) passes. The Bold/Italic overloads never verify the returned face is bold/italic — resolve('Arial',true,false) could return regular arial.ttf and pass; user gets a non-bold substitute where bold was requested.

If the resolver silently drops ALL unencodable codepoints (zero runs) when it should have routed them to a system font, the test takes the runs.empty() branch and calls SUCCEED(). The user's typed character renders as .notdef; the test passes as if correct. The strong FT_Get_Char_Index check only runs when runs are non-empty.

If the analyzer measures NO stem weights / NO x-height for every font (a total measurement regression), the loop finds nothing, skips all EXPECT_*, prints a cout note, and the test is green with zero assertions executed. Even with values present they're only range-bounded, not checked vs the fixture font's known metrics.

The visual re-ranking branch could be dead code (never invoked despite setBitmapCompositor) or re-rank to a worse font, and the test passes as long as confidence>0. It explicitly declines to distinguish the visual-ranking path from metric-only, so a regression disabling visual ranking is undetectable.

The serif-selection / font-size-capping / ghost-text bugs these target only run on one developer's machine (hard-coded C:/Users/dev/...SpecimenC.pdf); elsewhere they GTEST_SKIP, so a serif-for-sans regression or ghost-text reappearance ships undetected. Where they do run they assert only nonTransparent>0.

The test edits to 'Café résumé' but asserts only the ASCII skeletons 'Caf' and 'sum' survive round-trip. The accented codepoints é are exactly what font substitution exists to cover; if they drop to .notdef/tofu the user sees 'Caf' and this accent-specific test still passes.

Asserts QFont::italic()/bold() REQUEST flags, not that Qt resolves an italic/bold face or the overlay renders slanted glyphs. If no italic face is installed (or synthesis disabled), font.italic() stays true while the overlay renders upright — the exact 'overlay dropped italic' complaint — and the test passes.

These name a behavior (reject low-NCC glyph / pad narrow crop) but wrap every substantive check in if(atlas.contains(X)). If the glyph is wrongly absent or wrongly unpadded, the guarded EXPECT never runs; comment at 1499 concedes 'the key invariant is no crash.' The reject/pad/score logic can regress silently.

The test name promises 'undo does not restore redacted content after save' — a real confidentiality property — but the body never invokes undo and asserts only reopened->pageCount()>=1@114. If undo-after-save DID resurrect the redacted secret (a plausible UAF/rebind bug this project tracks), this test stays green.

Apply is asserted only by NO_THROW + marks-cleared-to-0@238-241. A redaction that clears the mark list and reports done but removes NO content passes. This is exactly the gap test_redaction_roundtrip's header cites; acceptable here only because roundtrip/edge_cases carry the real oracle — in isolation the manager's core operation is content-blind.

Toggling a layer invisible that does NOT hide its content on the rendered page (OCG /OFF never written to the PDF, or render ignores OCG config) passes — the test only reads back the in-memory flag it just set via isVisible()@96-97; the page is never rendered, no pixels checked. Hidden-content-still-visible = an information-disclosure escape for layered PDFs.

PrintEngine emitting a blank page, wrong page, or garbage passes: EXPECT_TRUE(result)@84 + fileSize>0@92 pass for any non-empty PDF. Content-blind within this file; mitigated only by the separate test_fidelity_r3_21 raster oracle.

Insert/remove verified by in-memory count delta only@271,392 (no save/reopen, no pixel/placement). An insert that adds the XObject but never references it in the content stream (invisible image) or places it off-page passes. Plus 27 GTEST_SKIP guards → whole suite SKIPPED-green when fixtures absent.

Wizard producing correctly-counted, correctly-sized pages that are BLANK (image decode/embed silently dropped): widthPt NEAR 300@77 checks only geometry, no render/pixel check confirms the source image is actually visible.

Named 'VerifyStream' but only checks hasOutputIntent()==true@112. A corrupt/empty/wrong-N-component or non-sRGB ICC profile still satisfies the boolean — a structurally-present-but-invalid PDF/A OutputIntent is never caught.

The only tests exercising real byte-budget eviction depend on a hardcoded absolute path to a private PDF on the author's Desktop@164 and GTEST_SKIP otherwise@228. On CI the eviction logic — the entire point of C2 — never runs, so an eviction regression ships green.

Invisible-text (Tr=3) edit that actually paints faint visible glyphs: imagesAreDifferent(...,0.05)@1797 tolerates up to 5% of pixels changing before failing; thin overlaid text on a busy scan stays under 5%, so a Tr-mode regression that makes OCR text visible passes.
Only asserts >0 non-transparent pixels. Wrong glyphs, mirrored text, wrong font, or a single stray dot all pass — no positional/shape/OCR check ties output to the input string.

A memory leak or heap-corruption in the PKCS7 signature-verification path (the code that decides whether a signature is trusted) is not caught -- the test loops 100x and asserts nothing; there is no allocation/RSS measurement despite the name. A signature-forgery or parser-OOB regression ships green as long as the process survives.

The PKCS#7 verifier is constructed and its vtable pointers checked non-null, but check_digest/check_certificate are NEVER invoked on real content. A verifier whose check_digest always returned 'valid' passes every test in this file. No tamper/negative crypto case at this layer.

Entire file's oracle is 'signing did not throw' plus grep-for-marker ('/Type/Sig','/DocMDP','/P 2'). No verifySignature is ever called. An invisible signature that reports VALID but whose digest is wrong passes all eight -- invisible signatures are a notable forgery/repudiation surface precisely because there's no visible appearance to prompt scrutiny.

Header states this locks signature byte-range preservation (UI-SIG-12), but a saveIncremental that corrupts or rewrites existing signature byte-ranges passes as long as it writes a non-empty file -> a broken incremental save that invalidates prior signatures ships green.

An annotation's position/size (/Rect) shifts or collapses on save -- a sticky note/shape reopens in the wrong place -- and every roundtrip test still passes, because no test asserts the reopened annotation's rect/geometry (only type, contents, color). Ink additionally only checks stroke count>=1, not the path.

The DocTimeStamp fixture token is validated only by first-byte 0x30 and string/hex greps; the TimeStampToken is never parsed, its TSA signature never checked, its message imprint never matched to the /ByteRange digest. A corrupted/mismatched timestamp that still begins with a SEQUENCE tag passes -> document-timestamp integrity regressions invisible.

These 'TSA response parsing' tests rebuild request/response with raw OpenSSL and round-trip i2d/d2i WITHOUT ever invoking PDFE's TsaClient parsing/verification. They validate OpenSSL, not PDFE -- a bug in PDFE's own TSA response handling (e.g. failing to detect a status=2 rejection) is not exercised.

Same masked-by-UntrustedChain pattern: OCSP 'unknown' handling and stale/expired rejection asserted only via EXPECT_NE(LtvValidated) on a chain never trustable -> a regression treating 'unknown' as 'good' or ignoring staleness would not be caught.

A genuine per-byte password-comparison timing side-channel with up to a 4.9x timing ratio passes (code allows 5.0x though the comment intends 2x). Conversely wall-clock noise over 5 iterations makes it flaky -- neither reliably catches a real oracle nor holds a tight bound.

Drag-resizing an annotation handle (or paste) produces no undo entry / no geometry change because the real SelectTool drag/paste path is broken: the test manually calls tool.annotationMoved(...)/annotationPasted(...) itself then asserts that callback fired. The production mouse path is never executed.

Right-click Reply or Delete in the comment panel does nothing (action not connected): the QActions exist with the right labels but wired to nothing. All four tests assert only objectName/label existence -> the dead menu ships green.

Stamp persistence proven only by counting annotations of type==Stamp (before+1==after). A stamp round-tripping at the wrong rect, with lost contents, or with no visible appearance stream would count and pass -> user's stamp could reopen blank or misplaced, suite green.

Asserts only r.ok==true; the comment explicitly waives verifying the XMP packet was written. A fixer returning ok but writing no /Metadata (doc still fails PDF/A in Acrobat) passes. Same at 211 (OutputIntent) and 218 (JavaScriptStrip) — none re-validate the specific issue cleared.

Asserts output file exists + result.targetLevel==PdfA_2b (echoes the input arg). File-exists says nothing about conformance; a conversion writing a non-conformant PDF/A-2b (missing OutputIntent, unembedded fonts) passes — despite this same file's validator tests proving such docs are detectable.

Name says 'ReturnsNonEmpty' but body calls getImageXObjectData then SUCCEED() — returned data never inspected. Returning empty/garbage image bytes passes. Identical for GetContentStreamDataReturnsNonEmpty (line 308).

Name promises signed-byte-range preservation but asserts only pageCount survives saveAs. A save that invalidates the digital signature (the whole point) passes; comment admits byte-level preservation is not asserted.

Comment claims 'extraction must return text' but extractPlainText()'s result is (void)-discarded — a font extracting empty/garbage text (the real bug for non-embedded/CID fonts) passes silently. Only exact pageCount + no-crash enforced.

Intends to prove scrolling to a lower-page annotation moves the viewport but asserts only currentPage()==0 (private scrollOffset_ uninspectable). A scrollToPdfRect computing wrong/no offset leaves the annotation off-screen yet passes; real check punted to a Python screenshot diff.

Calls refresh() x3 then SUCCEED() — asserts NOTHING. A refresh that duplicates rows or double-counts trust anchors passes silently; only an outright crash is caught. Surrounded by ~5 findChild!=null-only dialog construct tests (71/140/168/191).

Asserts pageMoved(0,2) emitted with correct args but never checks the QListWidget rows / document page order actually changed. A hook that emits the signal without performing the move (or to the wrong slot) passes.
Asserts only save time <30s + file exists. Never reopens to confirm the 500 form fields persisted. A save path dropping/truncating/corrupting fields but returning fast passes.

Computes grayDistinct vs lcdDistinct alpha-level counts to prove LCD carries more sub-pixel info for black text but only asserts each >1 and never compares them (comment: 'mainly a smoke test'). If the LCD path collapses to grayscale for black text, the test still passes.

Installs a capturing callback but never triggers a crash or invokes dispatch, then discards it; callbackCalled is never asserted true. If crash-to-callback plumbing is broken, the modal-suppression-under-automation behavior it guards silently regresses (the exact CI-wedge risk in project memory).

Enables file logging and asserts isFileLogging()==true + path getter, but never emits a message nor checks the file exists/contains the line. If file writing is broken while the flag flips, the test passes.

Asserts only that invokeMethod returns true (method invokable); never asserts the returned bool matches real print-enabled state. A broken isPrintEnabled() (Print greyed with a doc loaded, or enabled with none) is undetected.

EXPECT_TRUE(isUniform||hasGradient||isComplex||(!isUniform&&!hasGradient&&!isComplex)) is true for every combination of three bools; EXPECT_TRUE(fontFamily.empty()||!fontFamily.empty()) is a pure tautology. Any/garbage background or font classification passes.

Asserts glyphs.size()==5 and xAdvance>0. Wrong glyph IDs (renders wrong characters) or wrong advances (overlapping/spread text) both pass — nothing compares to expected glyph indices or metric-accurate advances.

PasteWithEmptyClipboard ends in SUCCEED() and only guards against a crash; a paste that corrupts span text or mis-fires the callback passes. CopyWithNoSelection reduces to EXPECT_FALSE(empty)+NO_THROW.

Cache test asserts only isNull-parity and (conditionally) equal size ('Either way, if we get a result, caching should work'); a cache returning a different/corrupt glyph on the 2nd call passes. StrokeWeight_NoOp asserts only result.size()==glyph.size() — a same-size blank/garbage image passes; pixels never compared.

After undo the page carries SOME image but not necessarily the ORIGINAL (wrong dimensions/content) — Oracle 2 asserts only !restoredData.empty(). Impact limited: Oracle 1 (191) covers dims deterministically.
Asserts only that a call doesn't throw and the window objectName()=="mainWindow". Any alignment-persistence defect is invisible.

The EXPECT_EQ(p.emitted,hex4(p.gid)) expected value is derived from fz_encode_character; if encodeGlyphIndicesHex maps cp->gid via the same MuPDF call this half is circular and misses a systematic shared mis-mapping. Mitigated: the EXPECT_NE(...,hex4(cp)) at 105 independently pins the real historical bug.

Asserts displayed 'ABC' is present but never that the /ActualText override is correctly ignored (a result that also leaked the override text as a separate run still contains 'ABC' and passes). Crash-regression coverage itself is sound.

Both tests are bare try/catch with ZERO assertions (L71-96). saveAs to a 300-char or UNC path could crash-recover into a silently corrupt/partial file and the test passes as long as it neither throws nor crashes; no file-state or exception oracle.
Name promises a throw on a path-less Document; body opens a normal doc and EXPECT_NO_THROW's saveIncremental() (L177). The defensive throw branch is never reached, so a removed guard is undetected.

EXPECT_GE(bookmarks.size(),0u) is always true on unsigned (L74); on the no-outline fixture the validation loop never runs (L35). A broken extractor returning garbage/empty passes as 'ran without crashing'.
Applies a reversed range (7,3) with a 'should not crash' comment but contains ZERO EXPECT_/ASSERT_. A silently corrupted run list from a reversed range is never checked — only a crash fails it.

Widgets can exist by objectName yet be disabled/unwired; a metadata dialog that displays fields but never pushes an EditMetadataCommand on OK (user's edit silently discarded) passes every test in this file — the dialog is never connected to a Document/save path anywhere in the suite.

The OCR oracle asserts invalidated.size()==3/ocred.size()==3 where those sets are filled by the command's OWN callback lambdas — it verifies the command re-invokes callbacks it was constructed with, not real document OCR state. A command firing callbacks but leaving OCR state stale passes.

Expected value is recomputed in-test using the same prof->ascender, the same synthetic fallback, and the same std::clamp(...,0.55,0.98) the production path uses. A shared bug in that clamp/fallback is invisible — actual and expected move together. Only partly caught by EXPECT_NE(actual,0.75).

Expected per-line sizes (2.4pt, 7.2pt) are the code's own x_size*72/dpi output restated as constants. A systematic error shared by the estimator and expectation (wrong ascender/x-height model that still scales linearly) yields the wrong on-page font size for every reconstructed line yet passes.

The name/comment claim it validates the missing-PANOSE fallback classification, but it asserts only fonts.size()>0. If the fallback mis-classifies every no-PANOSE font (serif<->sans flipped), this test still passes. The claimed fallback-correctness oracle does not exist.
Accepts any threshold in [20,230] for a bimodal image whose modes ARE 20 and 230 — essentially the entire meaningful range. An Otsu returning 21 or 229 (useless as a split) passes.

Manually emits the signal then asserts it was received@92-93 — proves only Qt's moc/QSignalSpy work; cannot fail for any product defect. The real contract (mouse selection triggers repaintRequested) is not exercised.
All 4 DPI tests GTEST_SKIP when the gitignored generated fixtures are absent@105 → on CI without gen_fixtures.py the DPI-detection metamorphic relation is never checked and the file is green.

Mislabeled DPI (e.g. '720' or a stray '72' from another field): dpiText.contains('72')@145 is a bare substring any string containing '72' satisfies; the pixel-dimension label was hardened with a regex@135 but the DPI label was left weak.

A read-only sticky-note popup still fires contentsChanged and silently mutates a locked annotation: despite its name, the test never asserts changedSpy.count()==0 -- only checks isReadOnly()==true. The no-emit guarantee is untested.

13 tests are PermissionFlags/EncryptionSettings/EncryptionInfo struct+bitmask echoes; they cannot detect any actual encryption defect (wrong algorithm applied, key not derived, password not bound). High assert density gives a false impression of crypto coverage; only bit-constant asserts (68-79) lock a real spec truth. Risk = mis-attributed coverage.

SEED RE-VERIFIED: the pure decompose/residual tests hardcode expected degrees and are NOT tautological. The real weakness is this integration test — it compares computeRunTransform(identity) to getTransform() only on integer .rotation/.scaleX fields, never a mapped point/quad. A shared translation/skew error leaving rotation/scale equal but placing reconstructed text at the wrong pixel passes.
Searches a +/-30px window (at zoom 1.0) for any red pixel of a 50x50 annotation. A ~30px positional error — clearly visible misplacement — still finds red and passes.
Comment says '>=5% must be non-white' but code asserts nonWhitePixels>0 — a page rendering a single stray dark pixel (99.9% content dropped) passes.

Asserts the name starts with the fixed prefix and is longer, but not that the suffix is the OS username. If it is a constant, two logged-in users collide on one single-instance domain and steal each other's file-open — the data-loss the class prevents.

notes.systemic_pattern: extraction-only-for-visual is the dominant cross-cluster disease (content-edit/TRE/fonts/redaction/image): a visual feature verified only by text-extraction round-trip, structurally blind to mirror/invisible/white/wrong-glyph/half-size/off-page — the exact class that shipped the mirror/half-size/color-loss content-stream defects.
notes.tautological_pattern: Multiple comment-labelled 'critical'/'regression-lock' tests re-implement the production formula in-test and assert against the copy, never invoking the product code path (Y-flip coord mapper, width-scaling, CID CMap loop, tile/HiDPI math) -> a revert of the real fix cannot fail them.
notes.security_theatre: cve_replay + malicious-PDF hostile-JS tests share a no-throw / wall-clock-timing oracle around a catch-all; signature trust-chain / DocMDP / OCSP-CRL rejections are masked by permanently-untrusted or self-signed fixtures; a live operator-precedence bug (&b==0) can no-op a tamper test.
notes.conditionality_escape: The strongest redaction byte/pixel-absence oracles GTEST_SKIP under secret-fixture absence / on Windows and STILL report green -> silent degradation to mark-count proxies; box-only redaction leaving Tj operators in the saved stream would ship undetected.
